Known gaps and follow-up work. Each item notes how it was found, so it can be confirmed before being acted on.

Unsupported SBML constructs

Algebraic rules in the three ODE-only targets

deSolve, MATLAB and Julia now emit a DAE and enforce the constraint. mrgsolve, rxode2 and ubiquity integrate ODEs only, so they still write the rule out as a comment, leave the species it constrains at a zero derivative, and warn. There is no fix short of solving the constraint symbolically for its variable and emitting that as an assignment, which only works for the cases where such a solution exists and is unique.

Two related gaps in what is implemented:

  • The DAE is only emitted when the number of algebraic rules equals the number of undetermined states (daeIsSquare()). SBML records no matching between rules and the variables they determine, and libSBML exposes none, so a model where the counts differ falls back to comments and a warning. A real bipartite matching over the variables each rule references would widen this.
  • Only species are candidates for what an algebraic rule determines (algebraicStates()). A rule that fixes a non-constant parameter or compartment is never matched, so the counts disagree and the model falls back to comments and a warning. SBML Test Suite cases 00182, 00184, 00573 and 00576 are all of this shape: parameters only, with rate rules and one algebraic rule. Another 19 (e.g. 00533, 00539, 00547) declare the compartment or parameter with no size or value at all, leaving the algebraic rule as the only thing that defines it; those are written as NaN with a warning naming the variable (warnUndefinedValues()).
  • Consistent initial conditions are assumed, not checked. inst/examples/sbmlalgebraicrules.xml happens to start on the constraint manifold. A model that does not will have daspk fail at t = 0, and ode15s reject the initial state; neither error mentions the SBML model. daspk’s estini can estimate them, but it requires the algebraic equations to come last in the residual vector, which the current row order does not guarantee.

Dilution for an assignment-rule compartment

A compartment with a rate rule is now integrated as a state and the species inside it get the dilution term -[S]*(dV/dt)/V. A compartment with an assignment rule gets the right volume but no dilution: forming the term needs dV/dt, i.e. a symbolic time derivative of the assignment expression, chain rule and all. All six writers warn in that case.

Doing it properly means differentiating an AST with respect to time and the states it reads. That is a real piece of work, and worth it only if such models turn up — no example has one. The SBML Test Suite has 18 (e.g. 00310-00318). Three of them (00310-00312) passed until assignment-rule variables became solution columns: the comparison then used the true volume rather than the declared one, which had hidden the missing dilution.

The warning also fires for a rule that does not vary with time (c = 1), where no dilution is needed. Silencing it means changing growing_volume_model(assignment = TRUE) in test-convert.R to a time-dependent rule first, since that test relies on the warning.

delay

SBML’s delay csymbol passes through unchanged, so inst/examples/sbmldelay.xml generates code that runs in no target. deSolve would need lagvalue(), and the equivalent per target. Only the ubiquity writer currently warns about it; the others emit it silently.

Events

Not exported at all — they appear only as a count in the generated header comment. getEventMath() can inspect them from R. inst/examples/sbmlevent.xml has two.

Miscellaneous maths with no target spelling

None of these is exercised by the example models, so all are untested:

  • Two-argument log(b, x). The Level 3 writer emits log(b, x), which is correct in Julia but reversed in R (log(x, base)) and invalid in MATLAB. formulaToUbiquity() already rewrites it as a ratio of SIMINT_LOGN.
  • root(n, x), exponentiale, factorial in C++, and the % modulo operator, whose spelling differs across R, C++ and MATLAB. (piecewise, ceiling, infinity and booleans are now spelled per target by rewriteForDialect().)
  • n-ary xor: R’s xor() takes exactly two arguments (00201, 00279).
  • The Level 3 Version 2 MathML functions – implies, quotient, rem, sec, arccoth and friends, n-ary plus written as a call – and the avogadro csymbol pass through unchanged and are not functions or names in R (about 18 suite cases, e.g. 01277, 01278, 01279, 00957, 00959, 00961).
  • The MATLAB ! -> ~ and != -> ~= rewrite in formulaToInfixMatlab() is reasoned-correct but unexercised: no example model contains a logical operator.
  • ubiquityUnsupported() lists the constructs named in the ubiquity documentation. Anything else — the trigonometric functions in particular — falls into the generic named-call path and is reported by name rather than being in the explicit list. ubiquity does have SIMINT_OR, SIMINT_NOT and SIMINT_NE, so or, not and != could be translated rather than flagged.

Smaller target-specific gaps

  • rxode2’s ini() block rejects an infinite parameter value; no spelling avoids that.
  • ubiquity maps a -inf lower bound to .Machine$double.xmin, the smallest positive double. Harmless for simulation; wrong for estimation.
  • MATLAB: a species named y or t overwrites the generated function’s own outputs. The parent function’s other locals are prefixed r2sbml_ for this reason, but t and y are its documented outputs.

Found by running the SBML Test Suite

Found 2026-10-17 by converting the semantic cases of the SBML Test Suite (https://github.com/sbmlteam/sbml-test-suite, cases/semantic/) to deSolve, simulating them and comparing against each case’s results.csv within its tolerances. That run is now part of the tests: 75 passing cases ship in tests/testthat/sbml-test-suite/, and the whole suite runs when R2SBML_SBML_TEST_SUITE points at cases/semantic, and in the sbml-test-suite.yaml CI job (pinned to suite commit d6dcd2c). Both fail below sts_pass_floor in test-sbml-test-suite.R; raise it whenever a fix passes more, and ship a case or two from that fix.

1011 cases are in scope (no events, delay, rateOf, fast reactions, stoichiometryMath or SBML packages). 647 passed at 4bc2da9 and 875 after fixing piecewise/ceiling/infinity spellings, three silently wrong conversions (assignment-rule compartment volumes, rule-set stoichiometry, conversion factors) and returning assignment-rule variables as outputs. The first harness put the scope at 766 because it read an empty packagesPresent: line as a package; the counts recorded with it in earlier commits (494, 526, 581) are low for that reason, though each before/after comparison stands.

The remaining 136 failures, by cause. The numbers are suite case ids, so each can be reproduced from the case directory of the same name; run the full suite through the helper in tests/testthat/helper-sbml-test-suite.R to see the current detail for each.

  • Algebraic rules (about 30): see “Algebraic rules” above. 18 of them stop the solver on a NaN written by warnUndefinedValues().
  • Assignment-rule compartment dilution (18): see above.
  • A species reference used in math, or stoichiometry that varies in time (13, e.g. 00974, 01107, 01449).
  • Level 3 Version 2 MathML functions and avogadro (about 18): see “Miscellaneous maths”.
  • A reaction id used in math as its rate (6, e.g. 01225, 01226, 01231, 01301): J0 is not defined in the generated code.
  • Conversion failed. (5, e.g. 00950, 01234, 01554, 01557). 00950 is expandInitialAssignments rejecting an initial assignment to inf/-inf/nan; the others are not yet diagnosed.
  • Conversion factors in the remaining shapes (4, e.g. 01484, 01499-01501).
  • Generated R that does not parse (about 12, “unexpected ‘>’” or “‘=’”); not yet diagnosed.
  • About 25 numeric mismatches not yet diagnosed individually.

Not action items, recorded so they are not rediscovered

  • libSBML 5.21.1 exists but is tagged prerelease and its only change is a fix to the Python bindings in the pip package. It touches none of the eight files patched by tools/cmake_call.sh, so upgrading is safe but pointless. Bumping the version means regenerating the bundled archive with tools/strip_libsbml_tarball.sh and re-checking every patch, since one that no longer matches fails silently.
  • R CMD check --as-cran reports 2 NOTEs, both benign: “New submission”, and a non-portable -mno-omit-leaf-frame-pointer flag that comes from Debian/Ubuntu R’s own default CFLAGS rather than from this package. The second does not appear on the CI machines.
  • A local check may add up to 4 more findings that are all environmental, not package problems. A missing inconsolata.sty (Debian/Ubuntu: texlive-fonts-extra) fails the PDF manual, which produces one WARNING, one ERROR (“PDF version of manual without index”) and a NOTE about the r2sbml-manual.tex it leaves behind; a missing tidy binary produces the HTML-manual NOTE. Install those two or ignore the four findings. The vignette checks — files in 'vignettes', unstated dependencies in vignettes, package vignettes, re-building of vignette outputs — all pass.
